pixel_inventory: One complete apparatus schematic, not multiple subfigures.
At the upper left are two separate DC input terminals, marked plus above the upper terminal and minus below the lower terminal. Their conductors end at separate fixed contacts near the selector.

At the upper right are two separate AC input terminals with a tilde between them. Their conductors end at the other two selector contacts. The upper AC conductor bends left and down to reach its contact.

The central selector contains six contact positions: four source-side fixed contacts and two load-side contacts below them. Two rising blade strokes are visibly coupled by transverse strokes. The coupling is apparatus structure, not a third electrical load branch.
The load-side left contact connects down/left to the bottom return conductor. The right load-side contact connects right through a single circular lamp with a crossed filament symbol.

After the lamp, the conductor enters the upper end of a vertically drawn coil at the far right. The coil's lower end returns along the bottom to the left load contact. Lamp and coil therefore occupy one series load path.
The coil has a repeated rounded-lobe winding stroke and a separate thick vertical core stroke beside it. Neither a resistance value nor a measured turn count is printed.
The source has no current arrow, inductor value, voltage value or frequency value. Plus, minus and tilde distinguish source types; they do not prescribe AC instantaneous polarity.
required_relationships: Two-pole source selection must retain both conductors of each source and common linked blade motion.
Keep the lamp and core-bearing coil in series on the selected-source load loop.
Do not turn the mechanical coupling into an electrical short between the two load conductors.

pixel_inventory: One unlabelled coil circuit schematic.
At the right are two separate source terminals, an upper terminal connected to the top conductor and a lower terminal connected to the bottom conductor. A tilde lies in the intervening gap.
The top conductor travels left to the upper coil connection; the bottom conductor travels left to its lower connection. The left-hand coil completes the external path between the two AC terminals.
The winding is represented by four visible rounded lobes. This is a schematic winding, not a stated numerical count of physical turns.
There is no lamp, selector, separate core bar, resistor symbol, current arrow, L label or numerical value in this source figure.
required_relationships: Keep one coil across one pair of AC terminals.
Keep the source-terminal gap; do not add a wire shorting those terminals.
Do not import the real demonstration's lamp, switch or core into this ideal-model figure.

pixel_inventory: One shared time graph with a vertical axis, an upward arrow, a horizontal axis with a rightward arrow and t at the right.
The upper-left axis labels identify u with subscript L and i with subscript L. A round origin glyph is printed below/left of the intersection; its inherited O/0 identity HOLD is not adjudicated.

A thicker solid curve is identified by an arrowed leader as i_L(t). It starts above zero on the vertical axis, slopes down, crosses zero, reaches a negative trough, crosses zero again, rises to a positive crest and ends above zero while descending.

A thinner solid curve is identified by an arrowed leader as u_L(t). It starts at the origin going negative, reaches a negative trough earlier than the thick curve, crosses upward, reaches a positive crest earlier than the thick curve, crosses downward and ends below zero.

At the thin curve's extrema the thick curve crosses zero; at the thick curve's extrema the thin curve crosses zero. Thin negative trough, thick negative trough, thin positive crest and thick positive crest occur in that order.
Both curves are solid; their weight distinction and leader-label bindings matter. There are no period ticks, amplitude numbers, units or measured coordinates.
The thick curve extends farther right than the thin curve. The source does not draw either curve through a complete second cycle.
The hand-drawn curves are not perfect harmonic interpolation and have unequal graphical heights. Equal drawn amplitude is not a printed equality between amperes and volts.
phase_relationships: With i proportional to cos(omega*t), u is proportional to -sin(omega*t), consistent with the plotted positive initial current and zero voltage turning negative.
Voltage leads current by a quarter cycle: corresponding voltage extrema occur before the current extrema of the same sign.
The source graph depicts voltage u, not the oppositely signed self-induced emf e_i.
required_relationships: Preserve the common axes, initial signs/slopes, order of zeros/extrema, solid line styles, thickness distinction and correct label leaders.
Retain unequal right-end extents and do not silently append cycles, ticks or measured amplitudes.
Regularized harmonic curves must be declared as modern ideal-model geometry, not as exact source pixel traces.
